subject: Mary, mother of Jesus
note: Evidence for Mary's Bible figure page. Scripture first (Luke 1-2, Matthew 1-2, John 2 and 19, Mark 3 and 6, Luke 11, Acts 1:14), all quoted from the BSB. Where the churches differ, each side is quoted from its own public-domain text: Catholic (Trent and Ineffabilis Deus in Schaff vol. 2; Munificentissimus Deus in Latin, our translation; Jerome; the Catholic Encyclopedia), Orthodox (the Longer Catechism, tr. Blackmore, in Schaff vol. 2; John of Damascus, tr. Allies 1898; the OCA for claims only, never quoted), Protestant (Augsburg Confession, Formula of Concord, Thirty-nine Articles, Second Helvetic Confession and the Waldensian Confession of 1655, all in Schaff vol. 3; Philip Schaff's own History and Creeds vol. 1; Calvin, tr. Pringle 1845). Every quotation is in mary-of-nazareth.quotes.json and verify-quotes exits 0. The texts are in design/saints-hub/sources/people/mary-of-nazareth/ (gitignored).

life.text: Annunciation at Nazareth; Mary 'a virgin pledged in marriage to a man named Joseph'; her question and her answer; Elizabeth in her sixth month.
Visit to Elizabeth; the baby leaped; Elizabeth's blessing; the Magnificat; stayed about three months.
Joseph's four dreams: to take Mary as his wife (1:20), to flee to Egypt (2:13), to return (2:19-20), warned to go to Galilee (2:22).
Birth at Bethlehem, manger, 'no room for them in the inn', shepherds, 'Mary treasured up all these things'.

Presentation: the sacrifice 'A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons'; Simeon and Anna. Leviticus 12:8 gives that offering for a mother who 'cannot afford a lamb' (used only in the evidence, not on the page as a claim about their means).
Magi 'saw the Child with His mother Mary'; flight into Egypt; Nazareth.
Jesus at twelve; three days; Mary's words (2:48); 'His mother treasured up all these things in her heart'.
Cana: 'They have no more wine'; 'Do whatever He tells you'; six stone jars; 'the first of His signs'.

His mother and brothers outside (Matthew 12:46-50; Mark 3:31-35; Luke 8:19-21); 'Blessed is the womb' (Luke 11:27-28). Augustine: 'Mary is more blessed in receiving the faith of Christ, than in conceiving the flesh of Christ.'
life.source: BSB; Augustine, Of Holy Virginity, chapter 3, NPNF 1/3, tr. C. L. Cornish

life.text: At the cross; 'Woman, here is your son'; the disciple took her into his home.
Last named in Acts 1:14, at prayer with the apostles, the women and His brothers.
life.source: Acts 1:13-14 (BSB); Britannica ('the last mention of her (Acts of the Apostles 1:14)')

life.text: Her words: six occasions in the Gospels (Luke 1:34; 1:38; 1:46-55; 2:48; John 2:3; 2:5). Counted in the BSB; Luke 1:40 has her greeting Elizabeth but gives no words.

John never gives her name (grep of John in the BSB: every 'Mary' is Mary of Bethany, Mary the wife of Clopas or Mary Magdalene). Matthew's genealogy names Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, 'Uriah's wife' and Mary (1:3, 5, 6, 16).
Galatians 4:4 'born of a woman': 'Probably the earliest allusion to Mary in Christian literature'.
Her name: of Hebrew origin, Miryam, 'the well-known proper name of the sister of Moses'; Greek Mariam or Maria; 'the name of six Christian females'.
life.source: Strong's Greek 3137, with Thayer's lexicon, Bible Hub

life.text: Parents Joachim and Anna; the donkey ('he saddled the ass, and set her upon it; and his son led it'); 'she was sixteen years old when these mysteries happened', with the note 'Six mss. have sixteen; one, fourteen; two, fifteen; and one, seventeen'; Joseph 'I have children, and I am an old man'.
life.source: Protevangelium of James, chapters 1, 9, 12, 17, tr. Alexander Walker, ANF 8 (ccel anf08.txt, fetched)

life.text: Magnificat: 'very similar in thought and phrase to the Canticle of Anna (1 Samuel 2:1-10)'; recited daily at Vespers; three Old Latin codices read 'Et ait Elisabeth' ('And Elizabeth said'), against 'all the Greek and Syriac texts'.
Hail Mary: first part Gabriel's words (Luke 1:28), second Elizabeth's (Luke 1:42); the petition 'Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners now and at the hour of our death.'
More than eight million signed petitions for a definition of the Assumption before 1950; 'there was a grave in Jerusalem that was said to be hers'.

Ephesus or Jerusalem: the Ephesus house found 'according to the indications given by Catherine Emmerich'; 'the evidence for her permanent home in Jerusalem is much stronger'. Also that the disciple of John 19:27 is St John.
Theotokos: 'giving birth to God, being the mother of God'; pronounced thē-ə-ˈtō-(ˌ)kōs.

fathers.text: Ignatius, Ephesians 19: 'the virginity of Mary was hidden from the prince of this world...'
Irenaeus, Against Heresies 3.22.4: 'the knot of Eve's disobedience was loosed by the obedience of Mary'.
Ambrose, Letter 63.110 (to Vercelli): 'When the apostles fled, she stood at the Cross...'
Calvin on Luke 1:48: 'we see how Mary makes herself nothing, and praises God alone.' (The same page goes on to criticise Catholic titles for her; the page quotes only this line.)
fathers.source: Calvin, Commentary on a Harmony of the Evangelists, vol. 1, tr. Pringle, 1845 (CCEL calcom31 txt)

fathers.text: John of Damascus, Dormition sermons: 'Thy pure and spotless body was not left in the earth'; laid in the tomb at Gethsemane, 'Then it was assumed after three days to the heavenly mansions.'
fathers.source: Tr. Mary H. Allies, 1898, Fordham Medieval Sourcebook

fathers.text: The Passing of Mary, First Latin Form (oldest ms. 13th century, per the ANF introduction): Thomas sees the body 'going up into heaven', the girdle, 'they did not find the body'.

churches.text: Council of Ephesus 431 condemned Nestorius, who preferred 'Christotokos ... “mother of Christ.”'

Cyril's (second) letter to Nestorius, read at Ephesus: 'they ventured to call the holy Virgin, the Mother of God, not as if the nature of the Word or his divinity had its beginning from the holy Virgin...'
churches.source: NPNF 2/14, the acts of Ephesus (ccel npnf214 txt)

churches.text: Chalcedon: 'born of the Virgin Mary, the Mother of God, according to the Manhood' (checked; not printed on the page in the end).
Formula of Concord, Epitome VIII.7 (Lutheran): 'she is both rightly called and in very deed is the Mother of God.'
churches.source: Schaff, Creeds vol. 3 (ccel creeds3 txt). LCMS calendar note on Cyril cites the same line.

churches.text: Ineffabilis Deus (1854): '...in view of the merits of Christ Jesus the Saviour of mankind, preserved free from all stain of original sin...'. Trent's decree on original sin excepts 'the blessed and immaculate Virgin Mary'.

Orthodox Longer Catechism: Q186 'She remained and remains a virgin before the birth, during the birth, and after the birth of the Saviour; and therefore is called ever-virgin'; Q187 Mother of God her 'other great title'; Q190 'honors her far above the cherubim and seraphim'; Q264 'calls upon Christ our true God, by the prayers of his most pure Mother and all his saints'; Q520 'his immaculate Mother'.
churches.source: Schaff, Creeds vol. 2, tr. R. W. Blackmore

churches.text: Patriarchal Encyclical of 1895, chapter 13: only the incarnation of Christ 'is alone pure and immaculate'; the 1854 teaching 'a novel dogma ... unknown to the ancient Church'. PARAPHRASED on the page, not quoted: the English on orthodoxinfo.com names no translator, so its public-domain status is not proved.

Schaff (Protestant): Mary 'calls God her Saviour (Luke i. 47...), and thereby includes herself in the number of the redeemed.' Only the last clause is quoted; the chapter around it is sharply polemical and is not quoted.
churches.source: Schaff, Creeds of Christendom vol. 1, section 29

churches.text: Jerome, Against Helvidius 21 (383, per the NPNF chronology): 'We believe that God was born of the Virgin, because we read it. That Mary was married after she brought forth, we do not believe, because we do not read it.'

Catholic reading of the brothers: 'His cousins or the more or less near relatives' (CE, 'The Blessed Virgin Mary'). CE 'Brethren of the Lord': the Helvidian view 'now adopted by most of the Protestant exegetes'; Greek Fathers: sons of Joseph by a first marriage; Latins: cousins.
OCA: James 'was the son of the Righteous Joseph before he was betrothed to the Most Holy Theotokos. Tradition says that Joseph had other sons with his first wife.' (Paraphrased on the page.)
Second Helvetic Confession, chapter 11 (English appendix in Schaff vol. 3): 'born of Mary, who was always a virgin'.

Schaff, History vol. 1: three theories; 'The first is now confined to Protestants, the second is the Greek, the third the Roman view'; the brother theory 'regards the brothers as younger children of Joseph and Mary', which he advocated.
churches.source: Schaff, History of the Christian Church, vol. 1

churches.text: Calvin on Matthew 1:25: 'no just and well-grounded inference can be drawn from these words ... as to what took place after the birth of Christ' (checked; left off the page for length).
Trent, session 25: 'that it is good and useful suppliantly to invoke them'.
Augsburg Confession XXI: 'the memory of saints may be set before us...' and 'the Scripture teacheth not to invocate saints...'.
Waldensian (Piedmont) Confession of 1655, additions, item 14: 'hold above all the holy Virgin Mary to be 'blessed amongst women.''
Thirty-nine Articles, VI: 'whatsoever is not read therein, nor may be proved thereby, is not to be required of any man, that it should be believed as an article of the Faith'.

Munificentissimus Deus (1950), the definition in Latin: 'Immaculatam Deiparam semper Virginem Mariam, expleto terrestris vitae cursu, fuisse corpore et anima ad caelestem gloriam assumptam.' English on the page is ours.

Second Council of Nicaea (787): images of 'our spotless Lady, the Mother of God'; 'honourable reverence ... not indeed that true worship of faith (latreian) which pertains alone to the divine nature'.
OCA Dormition: buried at Gethsemane; Thomas late, the tomb opened on the third day, 'only the grave wrappings'; 'bodily ascent'. Paraphrased.

feasts.text: Catholic (USCCB 2026): 1 Jan Solemnity of Mary, the Holy Mother of God; 25 Mar Annunciation of the Lord; 15 Aug Assumption; 22 Aug Queenship (not printed); 8 Sep Nativity; 15 Sep Our Lady of Sorrows; 7 Oct Rosary (not printed); 21 Nov Presentation; 8 Dec Immaculate Conception. The Visitation (31 May) falls on Trinity Sunday in 2026, so it is taken from the Calendarium Romanum 1969 ('31 In Visitatione B. M. V.').
Church of England: 25 Mar Annunciation (Principal Feast); 31 May Visit to Elizabeth; 15 Aug The Blessed Virgin Mary; 8 Sep Birth; 8 Dec Conception.
Episcopal (LFF 2022): 25 Mar Annunciation; 31 May Visitation; 15 Aug Saint Mary the Virgin, Mother of Our Lord Jesus Christ.
LCMS: 25 Mar Annunciation; 31 May Visitation (3-year series); 15 Aug St Mary, Mother of our Lord. ELCA: 25 Mar Annunciation; 15 Aug Mary, Mother of Our Lord.
OCA: 25 Mar Annunciation; 15 Aug Dormition; 8 Sep Nativity of the Theotokos; 1 Oct Protection; 21 Nov Entry into the Temple; 9 Dec Conception by St Anna; 26 Dec Synaxis of the Theotokos.
Coptic: 21 Tobi, Dormition of Our Lady (Tobi 1 = 9 January, so 29 January); 16 Mesori, Assumption of the Body (Mesori 1 = 7 August, so 22 August).
feasts.source: copticchurch.net synaxarium; shared/wikipedia-coptic-calendar.txt for the month starts

pictures.size: 1431 x 1800, from the Commons 1920 px thumbnail

Virgin Annunciate, Antonello da Messina, about 1475, Galleria Regionale della Sicilia, Palermo. Wide-screen gallery only.

pictures.rejected: Our Lady of Vladimir (Commons Virgin_of_Vladimir.jpg): faces clear but the ground around them is badly worn; the owner rejects worn pictures. Angelos Akotantos's Kardiotissa photos: CC BY-SA, not allowed.

could_not_verify: The translator of the 1895 Patriarchal Encyclical as printed on orthodoxinfo.com: not named there, so the page paraphrases it and quotes the Longer Catechism instead.

Miracles section left out on purpose: the Bible records no miracle done by Mary; the virginal conception is told in her life, and later apparitions (Guadalupe, Lourdes, Fatima) are outside a Bible figure page and not researched.
Patronages and her colours in art: no source fetched, left out.
Her age: the Bible gives none; the page reports the Protevangelium's figures only as a myth-check.

checked: Every quotation: verify-quotes exits 0 (100 printed, 85 entries).
Numbers: her words six times (Luke 1:34, 38, 46-55; 2:48; John 2:3, 5), three months with Elizabeth, three days, five women in Matthew 1. All right; none counts an absence.

Feasts against the fetched calendars: USCCB 2026, Calendarium Romanum 1969, Church of England, LFF 2022, LSB, ELCA, the OCA day pages, the Coptic synaxarium (21 Tobi = 29 January, 16 Mesori = 22 August).

Britannica's eight million signatures and the tomb in Jerusalem; the Catholic Encyclopedia on the Magnificat, Ephesus and Jerusalem; Thayer's six Marys; The Passing of Mary (Thomas brought from India, the girdle) in ANF 8.
Disputed things (Mother of God, the 1854 teaching, the brothers, asking her prayers, the Assumption and Dormition): each side in its own text, no winner in our voice.
Pictures: Commons licence tags read by API (Sassoferrato PD-Art, Lambardos PD-Art, Antonello PD-old-100-expired); the card looked at downscaled: face centred, eyes near 38%.
changed: Feasts, 31 May: the Visitation line now names the ELCA too (its church year lists 'Visit of Mary to Elizabeth' on 31 May).
left_for_owner: The writer's own questions stand: the two sentences in our voice (the Nicaea myth's last line; 'Christ saved her too, by keeping her from it'), Augustine's line at the end of 'Who is My mother?', and the paraphrased 1895 encyclical.
